# Rules

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs`. Edit the rule metadata in src/rules/, not this file. -->

bekci ships 26 rules. Severities are defaults; some rules raise or lower severity based on context (for example, `curl | sh` is high in a hook but medium in documentation).

## BK001

**Invisible Unicode characters** · `hidden-unicode` · 🟣 critical · prompt-injection

The file contains characters that are invisible to humans but read by the model: Unicode tag characters ("ASCII smuggling"), runs of variation selectors ("emoji smuggling"), bidirectional overrides ("Trojan Source") or zero-width characters. These are the standard way to hide instructions in a skill or rules file that looks harmless in review.

**Fix:** Open the file in an editor that reveals invisible characters (or run `cat -v`), delete them, and treat the source of the file as untrusted until you know why they were there.

**References:**

- <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2024/hiding-and-finding-text-with-unicode-tags/>
- <https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.00169>

Suppress: `--ignore BK001`, `"ignore": ["BK001"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK001` comment on the line.

## BK002

**Prompt-injection phrasing** · `instruction-override` · 🔴 high · prompt-injection

Text that tries to override the agent's existing instructions ("ignore all previous instructions", fake system prompts, chat-template tokens, jailbreak modes). Legitimate skills and rules files describe a task; they do not need to cancel the instructions that came before them.

**Fix:** Remove the text. If the file is from a third party, do not install it. If you are documenting prompt injection on purpose, keep the example inside a fenced code block (reported as medium) or suppress it with `bekci-ignore BK002`.

**References:**

- <https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/>

Suppress: `--ignore BK002`, `"ignore": ["BK002"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK002` comment on the line.

## BK003

**Instructions to hide actions from the user** · `concealment` · 🔴 high · prompt-injection

The text asks the agent to keep something from the user ("do not tell the user", "silently upload", "without the user's knowledge"). Hiding actions from the person running the agent is the signature of a malicious skill or a poisoned rules file.

**Fix:** Remove the instruction and audit what the hidden action was meant to do.

**References:**

- <https://invariantlabs.ai/blog/mcp-security-notification-tool-poisoning-attacks>

Suppress: `--ignore BK003`, `"ignore": ["BK003"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK003` comment on the line.

## BK004

**Instructions hidden in a Markdown comment** · `hidden-comment-instructions` · 🟠 medium · prompt-injection

An HTML or Markdown comment speaks to the agent. Comments are invisible in rendered Markdown (GitHub, skill marketplaces) but are read verbatim by the model, which makes them a convenient place to hide instructions from reviewers.

**Fix:** Move legitimate guidance into visible text so reviewers can see it; remove anything you did not write.

Suppress: `--ignore BK004`, `"ignore": ["BK004"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK004` comment on the line.

## BK005

**Downloads and executes remote code** · `remote-code-execution` · 🔴 high · code-execution

A command pipes content fetched from the network straight into a shell or interpreter (`curl … | sh`, `bash <(curl …)`, `iex (iwr …)`). Whatever the server returns at that moment runs with your privileges, and it can change after you reviewed it. Reported as high in hooks, MCP server commands and scripts, and as medium when it appears in instructions the agent may follow.

**Fix:** Download the script, review it, pin it by checksum, then run the local copy, or install from a package manager with a pinned version.

Suppress: `--ignore BK005`, `"ignore": ["BK005"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK005` comment on the line.

## BK006

**Obfuscated or encoded payload** · `obfuscated-payload` · 🔴 high · code-execution

Code is decoded at runtime and then executed (`base64 -d | sh`, `eval(atob(...))`, `exec(base64.b64decode(...))`), or a large encoded blob is embedded in an instruction file. Encoding hides what will run from anyone reviewing the file.

**Fix:** Decode the payload offline to see what it does. Legitimate tools ship readable source.

Suppress: `--ignore BK006`, `"ignore": ["BK006"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK006` comment on the line.

## BK007

**Destructive command** · `destructive-command` · 🟠 medium · code-execution

A hook, script, MCP server command or instruction contains a command that destroys data (`rm -rf ~`, `mkfs`, `dd of=/dev/…`, force pushes). An agent that follows the instruction, or a hook that fires on every tool call, can do irreversible damage.

**Fix:** Scope destructive commands to an explicit, safe path and require confirmation before running them.

Suppress: `--ignore BK007`, `"ignore": ["BK007"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK007` comment on the line.

## BK008

**References credential or secret stores** · `sensitive-file-access` · 🟠 medium · exfiltration

A skill, script, hook or MCP server references a location that holds credentials: SSH keys, cloud credentials, browser password stores, the macOS Keychain, crypto wallets or other agents' auth tokens. Few legitimate agent extensions need these.

**Fix:** Confirm the access is necessary. Narrow it to the specific file the tool needs and never combine it with network access in the same component (see BK010).

**References:**

- <https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/>

Suppress: `--ignore BK008`, `"ignore": ["BK008"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK008` comment on the line.

## BK009

**Known data-capture or tunnelling endpoint** · `exfiltration-endpoint` · 🔴 high · exfiltration

The text sends data to, or points the agent at, a service commonly used to capture exfiltrated data or tunnel traffic: request bins (webhook.site, pipedream), out-of-band testing domains (oastify, interact.sh), paste and file-drop sites, Discord/Telegram/Slack webhooks, ngrok and similar tunnels. Also reports `curl` commands that upload local files.

**Fix:** Remove the endpoint. A legitimate integration talks to its own documented API, not a generic capture service.

Suppress: `--ignore BK009`, `"ignore": ["BK009"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK009` comment on the line.

## BK010

**Reads secrets and sends data over the network** · `credential-exfiltration-chain` · 🟣 critical · exfiltration

The same component (one script or skill file, one hook or one MCP server definition) both reads a credential store and makes outbound network requests. That combination is everything a stealer needs, and is the pattern behind most malicious skills found in the wild.

**Fix:** Do not install the component. If you wrote it, split credential access and network access, and justify both.

Suppress: `--ignore BK010`, `"ignore": ["BK010"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK010` comment on the line.

## BK011

**Hardcoded secret** · `hardcoded-secret` · 🔴 high · secrets

A recognisable API key, token, private key or credentialed URL is stored in plain text in an agent config, instruction file or skill. Agent configs are copied between machines, committed to dotfile repos and read by every tool and extension that runs as you; instruction files are sent to the model provider.

**Fix:** Revoke and rotate the credential, then reference it from the environment instead (`"env": { "TOKEN": "${TOKEN}" }`) or a secret manager reference such as `op://vault/item/field`.

Suppress: `--ignore BK011`, `"ignore": ["BK011"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK011` comment on the line.

## BK012

**Credential stored in agent config** · `plaintext-credential` · 🔴 high · secrets

An MCP server or agent settings file sets a credential-looking environment variable or HTTP header (`*_API_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`, `Authorization`, …) to a literal value, or embeds credentials in a server URL. Complements BK011 for tokens with no recognisable format.

**Fix:** Move the value out of the config file: reference an environment variable (`${GITHUB_TOKEN}`), use the client's input/secret prompt support, or a secret-manager reference.

Suppress: `--ignore BK012`, `"ignore": ["BK012"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK012` comment on the line.

## BK101

**Agent approvals or sandbox disabled** · `permission-bypass` · 🔴 high · permissions

The agent is configured to run tools without asking: Claude Code `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`, Codex `approval_policy = "never"` with `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, and similar. A single prompt injection then turns directly into command execution on your machine.

**Fix:** Use the default approval mode, or an allowlist of specific commands. If you need unattended runs, do it in a container or VM without your credentials.

**References:**

- <https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/security>

Suppress: `--ignore BK101`, `"ignore": ["BK101"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK101` comment on the line.

## BK102

**Shell access allowed without approval** · `unrestricted-shell` · 🔴 high · permissions

A permission allowlist pre-approves every shell command (`"Bash"`, `"Bash(*)"`). Any instruction the model picks up from a web page, issue, README or tool result can now run arbitrary commands without you seeing them.

**Fix:** Allow specific commands only, e.g. `"Bash(npm run test:*)"`, `"Bash(git status)"`.

Suppress: `--ignore BK102`, `"ignore": ["BK102"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK102` comment on the line.

## BK103

**Broad allowlist entry for a dangerous command** · `risky-allow-rule` · 🟠 medium · permissions

A wildcard allowlist entry pre-approves a command that can reach the network, run arbitrary code or modify the system (`Bash(curl:*)`, `Bash(python3 *)`, `Bash(rm:*)`). Wildcards on these commands are equivalent to unrestricted shell access for an attacker who controls the arguments.

**Fix:** Replace the wildcard with the exact invocations you need, or leave the command on ask.

Suppress: `--ignore BK103`, `"ignore": ["BK103"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK103` comment on the line.

## BK104

**MCP servers or tools approved automatically** · `auto-approved-mcp` · 🟠 medium · permissions

MCP servers are trusted or their tools approved without confirmation: Claude Code `enableAllProjectMcpServers`, Gemini CLI `trust: true`, Cline/Roo `alwaysAllow`/`autoApprove`. A project you clone can then start servers you never reviewed, and tool calls driven by injected content run silently.

**Fix:** Approve servers individually and keep tool confirmations on for tools that write, send or execute.

Suppress: `--ignore BK104`, `"ignore": ["BK104"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK104` comment on the line.

## BK105

**Repository defines hooks that run automatically** · `project-hook` · 🔵 low · permissions

A project-level config file registers shell commands that the agent runs automatically on events (session start, before/after tool calls). Anyone who can commit to the repository can change what runs on your machine when you open it with the agent. Review these before trusting a cloned repository.

**Fix:** Read every hook command. Prefer checked-in scripts over inline shell, and review hook changes in code review.

Suppress: `--ignore BK105`, `"ignore": ["BK105"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK105` comment on the line.

## BK106

**Skill or command pre-approves unrestricted shell** · `skill-unrestricted-tools` · 🟠 medium · permissions

A skill or slash command pre-approves unrestricted shell access via `allowed-tools` (e.g. `Bash` without a command pattern). While it is active, any command runs without asking you first.

**Fix:** Restrict the tool to the commands the skill needs, e.g. `Bash(python scripts/convert.py:*)`.

Suppress: `--ignore BK106`, `"ignore": ["BK106"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK106` comment on the line.

## BK107

**Skill description tries to trigger on everything** · `greedy-skill-trigger` · 🔵 low · prompt-injection

Agents decide which skill to load from its `description`. A description that demands to be used for every task ("always invoke before any response") pulls the skill into unrelated conversations, which widens the blast radius of anything else the skill contains. Malicious skills use this to make sure they run.

**Fix:** Describe concretely when the skill applies. Only workflow skills you fully trust should be this broad.

Suppress: `--ignore BK107`, `"ignore": ["BK107"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK107` comment on the line.

## BK201

**MCP server runs an unpinned package** · `unpinned-mcp-package` · 🟠 medium · supply-chain

The MCP server is launched with `npx`, `uvx`, `pipx run`, `docker run` or a git URL without an exact version. Every launch fetches whatever is newest, so a compromised maintainer account, a hijacked package or a malicious update ("rug pull") executes on your machine automatically, with your credentials in reach.

**Fix:** Pin an exact version (`@scope/server@1.4.2`, `mcp-server-fetch==2025.4.7`, an image digest or a commit SHA) and update deliberately.

**References:**

- <https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/first-malicious-mcp-server-found.html>

Suppress: `--ignore BK201`, `"ignore": ["BK201"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK201` comment on the line.

## BK202

**Remote MCP server over plain HTTP** · `insecure-remote-mcp` · 🔴 high · supply-chain

A remote MCP server is reached over unencrypted `http://` or `ws://`. Anyone on the network path can read your prompts, tool results and tokens, or inject their own tool definitions and responses.

**Fix:** Use the server's `https://` endpoint. Plain HTTP is only acceptable for loopback addresses.

Suppress: `--ignore BK202`, `"ignore": ["BK202"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK202` comment on the line.

## BK203

**MCP server container escapes isolation** · `privileged-container` · 🔴 high · supply-chain

A Docker/Podman-based MCP server is started with options that remove container isolation: `--privileged`, host networking/PID namespace, dangerous capabilities, the Docker socket, or a mount of the host root or home directory. The server then has the same reach as a process on the host.

**Fix:** Drop the flag. Mount only the directory the server needs, read-only where possible (`-v "$PWD:/work:ro"`).

Suppress: `--ignore BK203`, `"ignore": ["BK203"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK203` comment on the line.

## BK204

**MCP server granted the whole home or root directory** · `broad-filesystem-access` · 🟠 medium · supply-chain

An MCP server receives `/`, `~` or your home directory as an argument, typically a filesystem server. Everything under it, including SSH keys, cloud credentials, browser profiles and other projects, becomes readable (and often writable) through tool calls that a prompt injection can trigger.

**Fix:** Pass only the project directories the server needs.

Suppress: `--ignore BK204`, `"ignore": ["BK204"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK204` comment on the line.

## BK205

**Look-alike of a well-known MCP package** · `typosquat-package` · 🔴 high · supply-chain

The package name is one or two characters away from a popular MCP server, or reuses an official package name under a different scope. Typosquatting is the most common way malicious packages reach developer machines.

**Fix:** Check the exact package name on the registry and in the vendor's documentation, then fix the config.

Suppress: `--ignore BK205`, `"ignore": ["BK205"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK205` comment on the line.

## BK206

**Skill ships a compiled binary** · `opaque-binary` · 🟠 medium · supply-chain

A skill directory contains compiled code (executables, shared libraries, `.pyc`, `.jar`, `.wasm`). It cannot be reviewed like the rest of the skill, and anything in the skill may tell the agent to run it.

**Fix:** Prefer skills that ship source. Build binaries yourself from the published source, or remove the skill.

Suppress: `--ignore BK206`, `"ignore": ["BK206"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK206` comment on the line.

## BK301

**Lethal trifecta: private data + untrusted content + exfiltration** · `lethal-trifecta` · 🔴 high · toxic-flow

Taken together, the MCP servers enabled for one agent can (1) read private data, (2) ingest content an attacker controls, such as web pages, issues or email, and (3) send data out. That combination is all a prompt injection needs to steal data; no individual server has to be malicious. Coined by Simon Willison; demonstrated against the GitHub MCP server, where a public issue made the agent leak private repositories.

**Fix:** Break one leg: do not combine these servers in the same agent profile, scope tokens to public data only, or keep confirmations on for tools that send data out. Use separate profiles for browsing and for private work.

**References:**

- <https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/>
- <https://invariantlabs.ai/blog/mcp-github-vulnerability>

Suppress: `--ignore BK301`, `"ignore": ["BK301"]` in `.bekci.json`, or a `bekci-ignore BK301` comment on the line.
